title: A course is more than its PDFs: building the materials exporter
description: How Study Kit 1.8–1.11.1 turns Moodle pages, Books, assignment briefs, Ed Lessons and linked Google files into a local course package, with offline PDF printing, isolated accounts and an explicit list of what is missing.
content:
The earlier Ed export article covered lesson folders and a download-all zip. A course has more than Ed files: a Moodle Page containing the brief, a Book with several chapters, a marking guide, pictures embedded in a lesson, and a Google document that is still only a link. Packing the PDFs already on disk leaves all of those behind.

Study Kit 1.8 added a whole-course package. Versions 1.9 through 1.11.1 filled in these gaps and added isolated accounts and PDF output. This article follows the current source and changelog. It describes the local exporter; private deployment changes and production verification are separate work.

Release update (3 November 2026): 1.11.2 is published, fixing Windows PDF browser cold-start retries. The commands below apply to the current release.



The demo runs offline against synthetic materials, deliberately retaining a missing attachment and an unauthorized Google link to show how omissions are reported.

Start with a useful command

After installing Study Kit and selecting your units:

monash export FIT2109 --sync --format both --to "./exports"


The destination is a folder, not a zip filename. --sync refreshes this unit’s Moodle content and Ed Lessons before packaging. It leaves Ed discussions out. Without it, export only reads the local cache. --dir writes a directory rather than a zip, and --open reveals the result in the file manager.

In 1.11.1 an interactive terminal opens a folder picker if --to is absent; --no-ask skips it. The starting location is the previous choice or the system Downloads folder, including a relocated Windows Downloads folder. The command prints the destination before work starts and progress while rendering and packing.

Collect first, package second

There are three stages:

Moodle / Ed / course-linked Google files
                 |
         sync and normalize
                 |
     local files + SQLite metadata
                 |
  export.Plan: entries + missing + statistics
                 |
       optional offline PDF rendering
                 |
    zip or directory, including an index


The code is split accordingly: syncer.py and moodle_content.py collect Moodle materials, the Ed modules collect Lessons, google_export.py handles linked Google files, export.py plans the package, and pdfrender.py prints its Markdown pages. Packaging does not need a live session unless the CLI was explicitly asked to sync first.

Moodle Page, Book and assignment bodies become Markdown. The Book parser uses Moodle’s print view, which does not count as viewing individual chapters. Visible rubrics and marking guides are teaching materials too; a student’s submissions, grades and private feedback are excluded. Moodle folders use a whole-folder download, retaining subdirectories and original filenames, with individual-file fallback when necessary.

Ed lesson pages contribute text, slides, embedded Ed-hosted files and question-only quiz pages. Images from Moodle and Ed are saved under assets/, deduplicated by content, and linked relatively. A failed image keeps its remote link and becomes an index entry. Older extensionless Ed images saved as .img are renamed from their detected content during sync, rather than remaining files a viewer cannot recognize.

The package has a unit root, Moodle/, Ed Lessons/ and an index. Original PDFs, notebooks, code and archives retain their formats. Generated bodies, link lists, quizzes and the index use the chosen output format.

A Google link needs its own permission

uv tool install --reinstall --refresh "monash-study-kit[gmail]"
monash google login
monash export FIT2109 --refresh-google --format both --to "./exports"


Keep any other extras you already use in that install command. The optional dependency happens to be named gmail; Drive authorization is separate. monash google login requests only drive.readonly and writes google-drive-token.json, independently of Gmail’s token. The scope can read all Drive files accessible to the account; the exporter uses course-linked files. It cannot edit them and grants no Gmail access.

Docs and Slides normally become PDF, Sheets XLSX, and ordinary Drive files keep their format. monash config google_docs_format docx changes Docs to DOCX. It does not change Slides or the exporter’s own Markdown pages. --refresh-google implies sync and re-exports linked Google files.

An API export can fail because of file size, a disabled API, administrator policy or sharing permissions. Where supported, the dedicated login browser’s Google session is tried as a fallback, with cookies held in memory. It does not bypass sharing permissions. Google Forms remain links with a reason. Logout revokes the Drive authorization before deleting its local token; failed revocation keeps the token so the user can retry.

PDF is another output, not another sync format

Since 1.11, pdf is the initial export default. --format md avoids PDF printing; both keeps editable Markdown alongside generated PDFs. Synced text and the MCP search index remain unchanged.

One isolated temporary Chrome, Edge or Brave process prints the package’s pages offline. Local images are embedded, raw HTML is escaped, and remote requests are blocked. Without a supported browser, export falls back to Markdown and says why in the index and terminal. Version 1.11.1 retries Windows temporary-profile cleanup so a browser helper briefly holding a file does not invalidate an already completed export.

The cache key covers printable HTML and embedded image contents. Replacing a local image therefore changes the key even if the Markdown is identical. Cached PDFs live under data/pdf-cache/; oldest entries are evicted above 500 MB. JSON output reports generated and cached PDF counts and the fallback reason. These are implementation limits, not performance measurements.

Account isolation belongs before imports

monash --profile exchange setup
monash --profile exchange google login
monash --profile exchange export FIT2109 --sync --to "./exports"
monash profile list


Paths are fixed when modules are imported. entry.py therefore chooses the profile before importing the CLI and service modules. Named profiles keep credentials, databases, materials and browser sessions under separate profiles/NAME directories. They force materials-only mode: no Gmail sync, attendance, Ed discussions or personal-calendar setup. They cannot configure remote serving, monash connect, or an independent data-home move.

Cleanup is deliberately a separate command from the default account: monash profile remove exchange. It revokes Google tokens before removing login sessions, keeps materials and databases unless --all is supplied, and preserves files if revocation fails. Ed API-token deletion remains a manual step.

Complete also means naming the gaps

The exporter records missing local files, unsynced Ed units, failed Google exports and remaining remote images. Notebook image references that are missing or differ only by case are reported too. A successful zip does not prove that every linked resource was downloadable. Folder refreshes are normally limited to once a week; refreshing Google is not a universal force-refresh switch.

The package excludes personal records and strips meeting-password parameters from links, but its contents are ordinary local files. They are not automatically public or safe to redistribute. Gmail is a separate optional feature: ordinary Gmail login requests gmail.modify, while --read-only requests gmail.readonly.

For this update, the local Study Kit suite completed with 663 passed and 10 skipped. Those tests cover synthetic export fixtures, Google errors, profiles and PDF behavior; they do not establish that every real course, Google account or Windows installation works. The bilingual export guide documents setup, options and retry steps. The practical check after exporting is still to open the index and inspect what was left out.

title: 一门课不只有 PDF：完整课程资料导出怎么做
description: 从 Moodle Page、Book、作业说明，到 Ed 图片和 Google 文档：Study Kit 1.8–1.11.1 如何把一门课整理成本地资料包，以及 PDF 缓存、隔离账号和遗漏索引为什么要分开设计。
content:
上一篇 Ed 导出文章讲的是 lesson 文件夹和一键打包。但一门课还有别的东西：Moodle Page 里的作业要求、Book 的几个章节、评分标准、lesson 正文里的图片，以及仍然只是链接的 Google 文档。把磁盘上已有的 PDF 压缩起来，这些内容还是没带走。

Study Kit 1.8 加了整课资料包，1.9 到 1.11.1 逐步补齐正文、图片、Google 文件、隔离账号和 PDF 输出。下面按当前源码和更新日志说明本地导出器的实现；私有部署改动和生产验证是另外的工作。

发布更新（2026-11-03）： 1.11.2 已正式发布，修复 Windows PDF 浏览器冷启动重试；下文命令适用于当前版本。



示例使用合成资料实际离线导出，保留一个缺失附件和未授权 Google 链接，展示索引如何报告遗漏。

先看怎么用

装好 Study Kit、选好课程后：

monash export FIT2109 --sync --format both --to "./exports"


--to 是目标文件夹，不是 zip 文件名。--sync 先刷新这门课的 Moodle 和 Ed Lessons，不同步 Ed 讨论区；不加时只读本地缓存。--dir 输出文件夹，--open 在文件管理器里显示结果。

1.11.1 起，交互终端不写 --to 会先弹目录选择框，--no-ask 跳过弹窗。默认上次选择的位置或系统下载目录，也支持 Windows 移动过的“下载”文件夹。同步前先告诉你存在哪，生成 PDF 和打包时显示进度。

先采集，再打包

整个过程分三层：

Moodle / Ed / 课程链接的 Google 文件
                  |
              同步与规范化
                  |
         本地文件 + SQLite 元数据
                  |
    export.Plan：文件项 + 遗漏项 + 统计
                  |
           可选的离线 PDF 渲染
                  |
           zip 或目录，附带索引


对应源码中，syncer.py、moodle_content.py 收集 Moodle 内容，Ed 模块同步 Lessons，google_export.py 处理 Google 链接，export.py 生成打包计划，pdfrender.py 负责把 Markdown 页面打印成 PDF。只有 CLI 明确要求先同步时，打包前才需要在线会话。

Moodle Page、Book 和作业正文存成 Markdown。Book 读打印视图，不计作逐章查看。学生可见的 rubric 和 marking guide 也是教学资料，但个人提交、成绩和反馈不进入资料包。文件夹优先整体下载，保留子目录和原文件名，失败再逐个获取。

Ed Lessons 则提供正文、幻灯片、Ed 托管附件和只有题目的测验页。Moodle 与 Ed 图片存进 assets/，按内容去重，再改为相对引用。下载失败时保留远程地址，并写入索引。旧版本把无扩展名 Ed 图片存成 .img 的，同步时按实际内容修正扩展名，让图片查看器能够识别。

包内按课号组织，下有 Moodle/、Ed Lessons/ 和索引。原有 PDF、notebook、代码和压缩包保留格式；生成的正文、链接列表、测验和索引则使用选定的格式。

Google 链接需要单独授权

uv tool install --reinstall --refresh "monash-study-kit[gmail]"
monash google login
monash export FIT2109 --refresh-google --format both --to "./exports"


如果已经使用其他 extras，安装命令里也要保留。可选依赖虽然叫 gmail，Drive 授权却是独立的：monash google login 只申请 drive.readonly，保存在 google-drive-token.json，与 Gmail 令牌分离。该权限允许读取账号有权访问的全部 Drive 文件，导出器实际处理课程链接；它不能改文件，也不授予 Gmail 权限。

Docs 和 Slides 默认 PDF，Sheets 是 XLSX，普通 Drive 文件保留原格式。monash config google_docs_format docx 只把 Docs 改成 DOCX，不影响 Slides 或导出器自己的 Markdown 正文。--refresh-google 隐含同步，并重新导出链接的 Google 文件。

文件过大、API 未启用、管理员限制、未共享给当前账号，都可能导致 API 失败。支持时会尝试专用登录浏览器的 Google 会话，Cookie 只在内存中，不能绕过共享权限。Google Forms 保留链接和原因。退出授权先吊销再删本机令牌；吊销失败保留文件，让用户能继续重试。

PDF 是输出格式，不是另一套同步

1.11 起初始默认输出 pdf；--format md 不打印 PDF，both 同时保留可编辑 Markdown。同步保存的文本和 MCP 搜索索引不变。

每次导出使用一个独立的临时 Chrome、Edge 或 Brave 进程离线打印，嵌入已有本地图片、转义原始 HTML，并阻止远程请求。没有支持的浏览器就回退 Markdown，在终端和索引解释。1.11.1 会重试 Windows 临时 profile 清理，避免浏览器辅助进程短暂占用文件时，把已经完成的导出判为失败。

缓存键包含打印 HTML 和嵌入图片内容，因此只替换图片、不改 Markdown，也会生成新的键。PDF 缓存在 data/pdf-cache/，超过 500 MB 时淘汰最旧项；JSON 报告生成数量、缓存命中数量和回退原因。这些是实现规则，不是性能测试数据。

账号选择必须早于 import

monash --profile exchange setup
monash --profile exchange google login
monash --profile exchange export FIT2109 --sync --to "./exports"
monash profile list


模块 import 时就固定路径，所以 entry.py 必须先选账号，再加载 CLI 和服务模块。命名 profile 将凭据、数据库、课件和浏览器会话隔离在 profiles/NAME 下，强制只导课程资料：跳过 Gmail、考勤、Ed 讨论区和个人日历设置，也不能配置远程服务、monash connect 或独立移动资料根目录。

清理从默认账号执行：monash profile remove exchange。先吊销 Google 令牌，再清登录会话；不加 --all 就保留课件和数据库，吊销失败则保留本机文件。Ed API 令牌仍需手动删除。

完整还包括说清楚缺了什么

索引会列出本地文件缺失、Ed 课程未同步、Google 导出失败和剩余远程图片。notebook 引用的图片不存在、或者只是大小写不匹配，也要报告。zip 生成成功不代表每个链接都能下载；Moodle 文件夹通常最多每周刷新一次，刷新 Google 不是对所有资源强制刷新。

资料包排除个人记录，并去掉链接里的会议密码参数，但导出后仍是普通本地文件，分享前要检查，不能因此视为可以公开转载。Gmail 是另一项可选功能：普通登录申请 gmail.modify，加 --read-only 才申请 gmail.readonly。

本次本地 Study Kit 测试结果是 663 passed、10 skipped，覆盖合成资料、Google 错误、profile 和 PDF 行为，不代表每门真实课程、Google 账号和 Windows 环境都已经实测。双语导出指南列出了安装、参数和重试方式。真正导出后，仍应先打开索引，看清楚哪些内容没有带走。

title: One download button, three codebases: zipping a unit's Ed materials
description: Ed Web could zip a whole unit's Ed materials and Study Kit could not, even though it already downloaded them. Closing that gap meant renaming files without downloading them again, catching attachments, a bug the tests had hidden, and deploying to a server that was not running what I thought it was.
content:
The question was simple, and I should have asked it myself. Ed Web has a button that downloads a whole unit’s Ed Lessons as one zip, sorted by week. Why doesn’t Study Kit have one, when it already syncs those files to your computer?

It did sync them. It just kept them in folders named after Ed’s numeric ids, like 39026/116285/201_Workshop 3 Slides.pdf, skipped files attached inside Ed pages, and had no way to hand you the lot. My private server version had the same gap, from the other side: the zip existed on its website, but Claude could not give it to you in a conversation.

This post is about closing that gap in three places: Study Kit, ed-digest (my server’s Ed sync), and the remote MCP server that connects them to claude.ai.

What it looks like now

$ monash ed export FIT2109 --module "Week 3"
已打包 FIT2109：3 节 lesson、5 个文件（0.0 MB）
  ~/Downloads/FIT2109 Ed Lessons (Week 3) 2026-11-01.zip


FIT2109 Ed Lessons/README.md
FIT2109 Ed Lessons/03 Week 3 - Editor-Modern IDE/07 W3 Pre-Class/Links.md
FIT2109 Ed Lessons/03 Week 3 - Editor-Modern IDE/07 W3 Pre-Class/02 Before class.md
FIT2109 Ed Lessons/03 Week 3 - Editor-Modern IDE/08 W3 Workshop/01 Workshop 3 Slides.pdf
FIT2109 Ed Lessons/03 Week 3 - Editor-Modern IDE/08 W3 Workshop/02 Workshop 3 Handout.pdf
FIT2109 Ed Lessons/03 Week 3 - Editor-Modern IDE/09 W3 Applied Session/01 applied3-starter.zip
FIT2109 Ed Lessons/03 Week 3 - Editor-Modern IDE/09 W3 Applied Session/01 Lab brief.md


That is a real run against synthetic course data; the CLI prints in Chinese because most of the people using it read Chinese. The same zip is one click on the local library page, and one sentence in an AI app.


  
    127.0.0.1:8766 · monash library
    
      
      
    
  
  The local library page with the new button. Moodle and Ed files for a unit now sit in one group. Screenshot of the real page, captured at 2x, with made-up course data.


Renaming files without downloading them again

Readable folders were the easy part to want and the fiddly part to ship. Everyone who upgrades already has a folder of PDFs under the old names. Downloading them all again would be slow and rude to Ed’s file server, so the sync looks up where each slide was stored last time and moves it:

def _move_old(old: str | None, new: str) -> None:
    if not old or old == new:
        return
    src, dest = FILES_DIR / old, FILES_DIR / new
    if src.is_file() and not dest.exists():
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        os.replace(src, dest)


The new path is <unit>/<NN module>/<NN lesson>/<NN title>. The numbers matter more than they look. Without them, Finder sorts “Week 10” before “Week 2”, and modules come out in the order of their database ids rather than the order on Ed, so the module number comes from the position of its first lesson. Unit codes need care too: FIT3162/FIT3164 is one unit on Ed, and a slash is a folder separator, so it becomes FIT3162+FIT3164.

The same move also covers a lesson that gets renamed on Ed, and files of slides that disappear are deleted along with any folder they leave empty.

Attachments, and a stable id for something that has none

Starter code usually is not a PDF slide. It is a <file> element inside a text page. Those are now downloaded too, but only when the link points at Ed’s own file host, and only up to 200 MB, because a link to a dataset is still a link.

Every row in lesson_files is keyed by Ed’s slide id, and an attachment does not have one. I wanted to reuse the table, so every reader of it (the library, search, the lesson reader) would pick attachments up for free. The id is derived from the URL:

def attachment_id(url: str) -> int:
    return -int.from_bytes(hashlib.sha256(url.encode()).digest()[:7], "big") - 1


Negative, so it can never collide with a real slide; stable, so the next sync finds the file it saved last time; and tied to the URL, so when a teacher replaces the file, Ed issues a new URL, the id changes, the new file is downloaded and the old one is cleaned up. PDF slides follow the same rule: a changed file_url forces a fresh download instead of keeping the stale copy.

The zip is built from the database, not the disk

The export does not walk the folder. It reads modules, lessons and files from SQLite, works out the readable path again, and adds a README.md with each lesson’s progress and Ed link, a Links.md for reading pages, and a list of anything that failed to download. Two things fall out of that: a student who exports before their first sync on the new version still gets a properly named zip, and a missing file is reported instead of silently absent.

A bug the tests had hidden

While wiring the button into the library page I found that the page had never listed Ed files synced by Study Kit itself. The code checked whether a path sat under the Ed folder, but the database stores relative paths, so the check always failed. The existing test passed because it inserted an absolute path. The fix is one line; the lesson is to write fixtures the way production writes data. There is now a test with a relative path.

Adding a tool without growing every conversation

Every MCP tool’s name, description and schema is sent to the model in every conversation, used or not, so the project keeps a budget: a test fails if the catalog grows past a size, and another pins the original tools’ contract with a hash. export_ed_lessons fits in about 360 characters, and none of the old tools changed.

It is also the first Ed tool that writes something, a zip in your Downloads folder, so it is not marked read-only. That had a useful side effect: remote mode only exposes read-only tools, so a ChatGPT connected to someone’s self-hosted Study Kit never writes zips onto their server.

The server side

My own setup is different. ed-digest syncs Ed on a VPS and already builds a per-unit zip for its website. Rather than write a second packer, the remote MCP server loads ed-digest’s site.py and calls the same two functions, so the zip from Claude and the zip from the website cannot drift apart. It has to load it by path, because import site would quietly give you Python’s standard library module.

Claude cannot reach a file on my server, so the tool returns a link:

def download_sig(rel: str, exp: int) -> str:
    return hmac.new(_download_key(), f"{exp}:{rel}".encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()[:32]


The signature covers the path and the expiry, so changing either gives a 403, and the ed-export/ prefix only resolves to zips sitting directly in the export folder. Because one repository now depends on two functions in another, ed-digest has a contract test that pins their names and parameters. If someone renames them, ed-digest’s own CI fails, not a student’s request on a Sunday night.

ed-digest also picked up the improvements from Study Kit: numbered weeks in Ed’s order and attachments in the zip.

The server was not running what I thought

The plan was “pull and restart”. Before that I checked the service, and the live connector was not running from the repository at all. A systemd drop-in pointed it at a release snapshot, releases/student-20261031-r2, with its own virtualenv. The repository on disk was four pull requests behind.

So the deploy followed the snapshot pattern instead:


  Hash every file in the live snapshot and compare with git. The running code matched main before my change exactly, so the release would differ from production by this work only.
  Record the old symlink target, the drop-in and pip freeze for rollback.
  Unpack the merged commit into a new release, install the new core into a throwaway virtualenv on the server and run the whole suite there: 150 passed.
  Upgrade the live environment, switch the symlink, update the build SHA, restart.
  Call the tool with the service’s own environment, then download the signed link from outside: 200 with the zip, and 403 with a forged signature.


Then I updated the repository copy too, which runs the timers and the SSH version of the server. The only package that changed in that environment was the core, which I confirmed by diffing pip freeze before and after.

Takeaways


  When renaming user files, move what is there. Downloading it again costs users time and costs the upstream server bandwidth.
  Something without an id still needs a stable one. Derive it from what changes when the content changes.
  Build exports from the source of truth, not from whatever happens to be on disk.
  Test fixtures should look like production data, or they will pass for the wrong reason.
  When one repository calls into another, pin the contract in the one being called.
  Before deploying, check what the server is actually running.

title: 一个下载按钮，三个代码库：把整门课的 Ed 课件打包
description: Ed Web 能把整门课的 Ed 课件打成一个 zip，Study Kit 明明已经把这些文件下载下来了，却做不到。补上它要做几件事：改文件名但不重新下载、把正文里附的文件也抓下来、修一个被测试掩盖的 bug，还有部署到一台跑的不是我以为的那份代码的服务器。
content:
问题很简单，本该我自己先想到。Ed Web 有个按钮，能把一门课的 Ed Lessons 按周打成一个 zip 下载。Study Kit 明明已经把这些文件同步到你电脑上了，为什么没有？

文件确实同步了，只是放在按 Ed 数字 id 命名的文件夹里，比如 39026/116285/201_Workshop 3 Slides.pdf；Ed 正文页里附的文件不会下载；也没有办法把整门课一次交给你。我服务器上的私人版本缺的是另一头：网站上有 zip，但 Claude 在对话里给不了你。

这篇讲怎么在三个地方把它补上：Study Kit、ed-digest（我服务器上的 Ed 同步），以及把它们接到 claude.ai 的远程 MCP 服务器。

现在是什么样

$ monash ed export FIT2109 --module "Week 3"
已打包 FIT2109：3 节 lesson、5 个文件（0.0 MB）
  ~/Downloads/FIT2109 Ed Lessons (Week 3) 2026-11-01.zip


FIT2109 Ed Lessons/README.md
FIT2109 Ed Lessons/03 Week 3 - Editor-Modern IDE/07 W3 Pre-Class/Links.md
FIT2109 Ed Lessons/03 Week 3 - Editor-Modern IDE/07 W3 Pre-Class/02 Before class.md
FIT2109 Ed Lessons/03 Week 3 - Editor-Modern IDE/08 W3 Workshop/01 Workshop 3 Slides.pdf
FIT2109 Ed Lessons/03 Week 3 - Editor-Modern IDE/08 W3 Workshop/02 Workshop 3 Handout.pdf
FIT2109 Ed Lessons/03 Week 3 - Editor-Modern IDE/09 W3 Applied Session/01 applied3-starter.zip
FIT2109 Ed Lessons/03 Week 3 - Editor-Modern IDE/09 W3 Applied Session/01 Lab brief.md


这是用编造的课程数据真实跑出来的结果。同样的 zip，在本机课件页上点一下就有，在 AI 软件里说一句也行。


  
    127.0.0.1:8766 · monash library
    
      
      
    
  
  加了按钮的本机课件页。同一门课的 Moodle 和 Ed 文件现在放在同一组。真实页面的 2 倍截图，课程数据是编的。


改名，但不重新下载

文件夹名好读，是最容易想要、也最麻烦落地的部分。每个升级的人手里都已经有一堆按旧名字存的 PDF。全部重新下载又慢，又给 Ed 的文件服务器添负担。所以同步时先查这一页上次存在哪，直接挪过去：

def _move_old(old: str | None, new: str) -> None:
    if not old or old == new:
        return
    src, dest = FILES_DIR / old, FILES_DIR / new
    if src.is_file() and not dest.exists():
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        os.replace(src, dest)


新路径是 课号/NN 模块/NN lesson/NN 标题。前面的编号比看上去重要：不加的话，访达会把 Week 10 排在 Week 2 前面；模块按数据库 id 排，也不一定是 Ed 上的顺序。所以模块编号取它第一节 lesson 在 Ed 上的位置。课号也要处理：FIT3162/FIT3164 在 Ed 上是一门课，但斜杠是路径分隔符，所以变成 FIT3162+FIT3164。

Ed 上给 lesson 改了名，也走同一套挪动。页删了，本地文件跟着删，删空的文件夹也一起清掉。

附件，以及给没有 id 的东西一个稳定的 id

starter code 通常不是一页 PDF，而是文字页里的一个 <file>。现在这些也会下载，但只限 Ed 自己的文件服务器上的链接，单个不超过 200 MB。毕竟一个指向数据集的链接，终归只是个链接。

lesson_files 每一行都以 Ed 的 slide id 为键，附件没有这个 id。我想沿用这张表，这样课件页、全文搜索、lesson 阅读器这些读它的地方就都自动认得附件。所以 id 由 URL 算出来：

def attachment_id(url: str) -> int:
    return -int.from_bytes(hashlib.sha256(url.encode()).digest()[:7], "big") - 1


负数，永远不会和真的 slide 撞；固定，下次同步能找到上次存的文件；和 URL 绑在一起，老师换了文件，Ed 会给一个新 URL，id 随之改变，新文件被下载，旧的被清掉。PDF 页也用同样的规则：file_url 变了就重新下载，不再留着旧版本。

zip 从数据库生成，不从磁盘

打包不去遍历文件夹，而是从 SQLite 读模块、lesson 和文件，重新算出好读的路径，再写一个 README.md（每节的进度和 Ed 链接、没下载到的文件），阅读网页写进 Links.md。这样有两个好处：升级后还没同步就导出，zip 里的名字也是对的；文件缺了会写出来，而不是悄悄不见。

一个被测试掩盖的 bug

把按钮接进课件页时，我发现这个页面其实从来没列出过 Study Kit 自己同步的 Ed 文件。代码判断路径是否在 Ed 文件夹里，可数据库存的是相对路径，所以永远判断失败。原来的测试能过，是因为它插进去的是绝对路径。修起来只要一行；教训是测试数据要按生产环境写数据的方式来造。现在多了一个用相对路径的测试。

加一个工具，但不让每次对话都变长

每个 MCP 工具的名字、说明和参数，每次对话都会整份发给模型，用不用都算。所以项目里有预算：工具清单超过一定大小测试就失败，原有工具的契约还用哈希钉住。export_ed_lessons 大约 360 个字符，老工具一个字没改。

它也是第一个会写东西的 Ed 工具（往你的“下载”文件夹写一个 zip），所以没有标成只读。这带来一个好处：远程模式只提供只读工具，所以连到别人自建 Study Kit 的 ChatGPT，永远不会往对方服务器上写 zip。

服务器那边

我自己的部署不一样。ed-digest 在 VPS 上同步 Ed，本来就会给网站的每门课打一个 zip。与其再写一个打包器，远程 MCP 服务器直接加载 ed-digest 的 site.py，调用同样的两个函数，这样 Claude 给的 zip 和网站上的 zip 不可能对不上。它必须按文件路径加载，因为 import site 会悄悄拿到 Python 标准库里的 site。

Claude 拿不到我服务器上的文件，所以工具返回一个链接：

def download_sig(rel: str, exp: int) -> str:
    return hmac.new(_download_key(), f"{exp}:{rel}".encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()[:32]


签名同时覆盖路径和过期时间，改哪个都是 403；ed-export/ 前缀只能解析到导出文件夹里直接放着的 zip。现在一个仓库依赖另一个仓库的两个函数，所以 ed-digest 加了契约测试，钉住它们的名字和参数。谁改了名字，失败的是 ed-digest 自己的 CI，而不是某个同学周日晚上的一次请求。

ed-digest 也顺带吃到了 Study Kit 的改进：周文件夹按 Ed 上的顺序编号，zip 里有附件。

服务器跑的不是我以为的那份

原计划是拉代码、重启。动手前我看了一眼服务配置，线上的连接器根本不是从仓库跑的：一个 systemd drop-in 把它指向了一个发布快照 releases/student-20261031-r2，用的是另一个 virtualenv。磁盘上的仓库落后了四个 PR。

所以部署改成按快照的方式来：


  把线上快照里每个文件算哈希，和 git 对比。运行中的代码和我改动之前的 main 完全一致，所以新版本和线上的差别只有这次的工作。
  记下旧的软链接目标、drop-in 和 pip freeze，用来回滚。
  把合并后的提交解到新的 release 目录，在服务器上用一个临时 virtualenv 装新的核心包，跑完整测试：150 个通过。
  升级线上环境，切换软链接，更新构建 SHA，重启。
  用服务自己的环境调用一次工具，再从外网下载签名链接：正常的拿到 zip（200），伪造签名的返回 403。


之后我也更新了仓库那一份，它跑定时任务和 SSH 版的服务器。这个环境里唯一变化的包是核心包，我用前后两次 pip freeze 的差异确认过。

几点体会


  改用户文件的名字时，挪已有的。重新下载既耽误用户，也消耗上游服务器的带宽。
  没有 id 的东西也需要稳定的 id。从“内容变了它就变”的东西里推出来。
  导出要从唯一可信的数据源生成，而不是磁盘上碰巧有什么。
  测试数据要像生产数据，不然测试会因为错误的理由通过。
  一个仓库调用另一个仓库时，在被调用的那边钉住契约。
  部署之前，先确认服务器实际在跑什么。


后续：整课导出系统补上了 Moodle 正文、Google 文件、PDF 与隔离账号。

title: Why I want alerts about changes, not an endless stream of pings
description: Monitoring Linux nodes isn't just about running checks on a schedule. State, recovery and safe limits make alerts useful.
content:
With several Linux machines running separately, the obvious first monitor is a scheduled SSH check: inspect disks and containers and send a message if something looks wrong.

That is straightforward to write. After a while, though, a single persistent failure can send dozens of identical notifications. More alerts can make it easier to miss the one that matters.

Store state, not just snapshots

Edge Fleet Ops Automation is a sanitized reconstruction of tools I used for Linux edge nodes. Its useful ideas are node discovery, health checks, persistent state and deduplicated alerts—not one particular SSH command.

The first disk-space threshold crossing should be visible. Ten subsequent checks shouldn’t repeat the same message. Recovery is also an event worth reporting. Consecutive failures can reduce noisy actions during brief network drops.

Automatic repair needs limits

Removing files, restarting services or reclaiming disk space can be automated, but an incorrect action may make an incident worse. I’d rather use dry-run first, scope operations narrowly and decide which changes really can be unattended.

The public repository doesn’t imply that every tool is deployed on my current J1900 or N1 boxes. It’s a record of the engineering patterns I want to reuse as I rebuild their monitoring.

title: 服务器告警最怕什么都说，最后什么都没告诉我
description: Linux巡检不只是定时执行命令：需要区分新故障、持续故障和恢复，并为自动修复设置边界。
content:
几台Linux机器分开运行时，最容易想到的监控办法是每隔几分钟SSH进去检查一下磁盘和进程，再把不正常的结果发到手机。

这个方案初期很好写，实际用久了会遇到另一个问题：同一个故障，每次检查都发一次。到了后来，通知越多，我反而越容易漏掉真正值得处理的变化。

把状态记下来

我以前做的Edge Fleet Ops Automation是从一套真实用过的节点巡检工具整理出来的脱敏版本。里面的重点不是某个SSH命令，而是节点发现、健康检查、持续状态和去重告警。

如果一块盘第一次超过阈值，值得提醒；继续超标十次不需要十条完全相同的信息。恢复正常时反而应该有一条明确的恢复通知。临时网络抖动也可以通过连续失败次数判断，不要一次超时就启动修复。

自动处理应该保守

清理缓存、重启服务或回收空间看起来可以自动化，但每一步都可能删错东西或放大故障。我倾向先dry-run、限制操作范围，再决定哪些动作真的可以无人值守。

仓库中的公开代码不是我现在所有设备上的实时部署。它保留的是处理这类问题的思路，也方便我以后给J1900和N1重新搭建监控时作参考。

title: What SecureView's concurrency tests caught that a demo didn't
description: Connection-pool exhaustion and deadlocks became real questions only when the encrypted file-sharing app handled concurrent use.
content:
In a one-person SecureView demo, the visible features were encryption, upload, sharing and decryption. Later, I spent more time on less visible work: database connections, concurrent requests and what happens after a failure.

SecureView was our four-person final-year project. My work included testing, CI, deployment and security features. Correct encryption alone doesn’t make a file-sharing service usable under load.

Upload failures aren’t always crypto failures

A capacity test with 100 users exposed a connection-pool problem. Upload failures were substantial before the issue was diagnosed and fixed; the project’s README records the test results. I’m not presenting a fresh benchmark in this post.

We also encountered MySQL concurrency deadlocks. These bugs often involve transaction boundaries and lock ordering rather than the most complicated business function. A successful single upload exercises none of that contention.

Leave a regression test behind

After fixing a concurrency bug, I want a test that recreates the failure. A few successful manual retries aren’t enough. The MySQL suite, browser tests and fault-injection cases help protect against regressions.

A deadlock error by itself isn’t a complete diagnosis. It matters which statements lock which rows, how retries work, and whether a write’s outcome is known.

See the SecureView repository for historical measurements and environment notes. This is a retrospective on testing, not a new performance claim about the current deployment.

title: SecureView的并发测试为什么比单人演示更重要
description: 连接池耗尽和数据库死锁，是加密文件分享系统在多用户情况下必须认真检查的问题。
content:
SecureView在单人演示时，最容易看见的是加密上传、分享和解密。但项目做到后面，我花了更多时间在没那么显眼的地方：数据库连接、并发请求和失败后的恢复。

这是我们四人的毕业设计。我负责的部分包括测试、CI、部署和一些安全功能。加密文件分享不仅要保证算法正确，还要保证请求多的时候不会把数据库卡死。

上传失败不一定是加密出错

我们做过多人并发的容量测试，发现100用户场景下数据库连接池的问题。上传失败率一度很高，排查后修复了连接池故障；项目README里保留了对应的测试记录。这里不重新给出没有运行过的新基准。

同一类问题还包括MySQL并发死锁。错误不一定出现在最复杂的业务逻辑里，有时是多个请求以不同顺序争抢行锁。只测试一次上传成功，完全看不出这些路径。

我后来更依赖回归测试

修复以后，应该留下能够复现故障的测试，而不是只在本地重试几次就算解决。MySQL相关测试、真实浏览器流程和故障注入，都是为了让今后的改动不要把同类问题带回来。

数据库问题不宜只凭一个错误码下结论。要看具体事务、锁顺序、超时和重试边界，尤其不能对结果未知的写操作无限重试。

项目的具体环境、历史测试数字与限制，都放在SecureView仓库。这篇文章只是整理为什么需要并发测试，不等于对当前线上环境重新做过性能验收。

title: Why I built a degree planner for Monash students
description: Putting units into semesters is easy. Checking prerequisites, campus and offering periods against the Handbook is the harder part.
content:
The annoying part of planning a Monash degree isn’t entering unit codes. It’s checking whether each unit is available at your campus, whether it runs in the semester you chose and whether its prerequisites can be completed beforehand.

A spreadsheet can hold a plan. It doesn’t automatically verify those constraints. That gap is one reason I built Monash Hub.

Keep the plan local; verify against the source

Students can drag units between terms, undo changes and export their plans. When they ask the app to check a plan, the relevant entries go to an API backed by the Handbook data. The server doesn’t need to keep a permanent copy of the personal plan.

The distinction between “not found” and “not allowed” matters. Missing a unit for a year in the local dataset doesn’t prove the unit was cancelled. A prerequisite warning also needs a reason and a way back to the official source.

A warning is not a university ruling

The tool cannot approve a prerequisite exemption, overseas credit transfer or graduation. It can identify possible conflicts early and point the student to the relevant Handbook entry.

Sometimes its most useful answer is not a green check, but a specific question the student knows to take to the faculty.

The source shows the current plan model and rule checks. Comparing different Handbook years properly is still an area for improvement; I don’t want newer rules silently replacing what applied to an older study plan.

title: 我为什么做了Monash选课规划工具
description: 把课程摆进学期表不难，难的是检查先修要求、校区和开课学期，且每条结论都要有Handbook来源。
content:
选课时最烦的并不是填几个课程代码，而是反复确认：这门课在马来西亚开吗？有没有先修？明年这个学期会不会不开？

手动做Excel表当然可以，但一旦要考虑先修顺序、不同学期的开课情况和学位结构，一个格子填错就可能影响后面的计划。这也是我开始做Monash Hub的原因之一。

计划可以在本地，规则不能随口猜

目前的计划表可以在浏览器里编辑、移动课程和撤销操作。检查时，会把需要核对的课程安排发送给API，对照已经收录的Handbook数据。服务端不需要替学生保存整张个人学位计划。

我特别在意“没有资料”和“不符合要求”的区别。如果某个年份没有收录某门课，不能直接当作这门课不开；如果某个课程与学位要求有冲突，也不应该只显示一个红色图标却不给出处。

学位规划不是正式选课审核

学校最终如何批准先修豁免、交换学分和毕业资格，仍以学校流程为准。工具能做的是提早暴露可能的问题，并且让人可以打开原始Handbook核对。

最有用的一次检查，可能不是告诉你“全部通过”，而是指出某门必修课只在某个学期开课，接下来应该去确认什么。

项目源码有当前的计划数据结构与检查逻辑。我还在补不同Handbook年份之间的差异对比，这项功能不能只拿最新一年替代全部历史规则。

title: Why I use Jekyll but serve the blog from my own VPS
description: Writing, building and serving a static blog are different jobs. GitHub Pages remains a mirror; the VPS serves the main domain.
content:
I was tempted to make the blog a full web app. More projects, better navigation and search can all make a database-backed rewrite sound appealing. But the thing this site does most is still simple: it turns Markdown into pages.

I kept Jekyll. It already handles posts, layouts, feeds and the sitemap. Chinese and English versions share a reference so readers can switch languages. A nicer portfolio homepage didn’t require throwing that away.

Building and serving are separate jobs

The source lives in waldo0926.github.io. GitHub Actions builds the static site into a dedicated site branch. My VPS pulls those generated files on a schedule and serves blog.secureview.tech.

Visitors don’t need the Jekyll toolchain running on the VPS. The GitHub Pages address stays available as a separate mirror. Two working URLs are useful, but I wouldn’t call that automatic failover.

Small publishing pipelines still break

One accidental broken template can take down an entire page. I added PR checks for the Jekyll build and the social preview images, rather than discovering missing assets after publishing.

Links are the other maintenance cost. Bilingual posts must point to each other, and the project archive needs the same treatment. Domain or navigation changes can break these relationships without touching a line of application code.

The repository documents the current workflow. This post records how the blog is built today, not a promise that its deployment will never change.

title: 为什么博客用Jekyll，网站却放在自己的VPS上
description: 把写文章、构建静态页面和实际部署分开，GitHub Pages作为镜像，而不是让博客依赖一台服务器。
content:
以前想把博客做复杂一点：写文章、展示项目、加搜索，似乎很容易一路做成需要数据库的Web应用。但博客最常做的事其实只有一件：把Markdown变成网页。

我最后继续用了Jekyll。它已经能处理文章、布局、RSS和站点地图，英文和中文文章用同一个ref配对。没有必要因为想要更好看的首页就把整套系统换掉。

GitHub负责构建，VPS负责提供网页

网站源码放在waldo0926.github.io。GitHub Actions根据源码构建静态文件，放到专门的site分支。VPS定时拉取这个分支，通过自己的Web服务把内容放在blog.secureview.tech。

这样一来，线上不需要安装整套Jekyll运行环境，也不需要让访问博客的用户接触构建工具。GitHub Pages地址还在，可以作为独立镜像查看。两条发布路径应该保持内容一致，但我不会因为它们都能打开，就把它们称为自动故障切换。

一个简单的发布流程也有坑

静态站点最怕的不是查询慢，而是把坏的HTML直接发布出去。所以我给PR补了构建检查，还校验文章分享图的路径是否真的存在。合并前先让Jekyll构建，胜过部署后才看到页面空白。

另一个容易忘的地方是链接。每篇中文文章需要对应的英文地址，项目档案也一样。换域名、增加分类或重排目录时，内部链接和分享卡片都可能跟着出问题。

代码和当前发布流程可以在博客仓库看。这篇记录的是已有设计；如果之后换部署方式，应该再更新文章，而不是让读者按旧说明操作。

title: The string algorithms I kept after the course ended
description: A post-course rebuild of Z matching, BWT search, Ukkonen suffix trees and Rabin–Karp, including the limitations I don't want to hide behind complexity claims.
content:
When I revisited my algorithms coursework, I didn’t want to dump the old assignment directory straight onto GitHub. The code might still run, but without the design choices, complexity notes and boundary tests, it wouldn’t mean much to someone else—or to me a year later.

I pulled four areas into a standalone Python repository: Z-based exact matching, BWT-backed approximate matching, Ukkonen suffix trees with LCP extraction, and Rabin–Karp with Miller–Rabin prime generation.

What the repository isn’t

It isn’t a production search engine. The BWT example deliberately has a simple suffix-array builder. The Z matcher has an O(m²) shift-preprocessing step in this implementation. Describing either as simply a “fast text-search algorithm” would hide a real cost.

Ukkonen’s suffix tree is another good example. It’s easy to mention linear-time construction, but the mistakes I kept looking for were in the active point, suffix links and skip/count bookkeeping. I wanted the implementation to make those transitions inspectable.

How I check the results

For BWT approximate matching, the test cases separate substitution, insertion, deletion and transposition. For the LCP array, I compare against a naive reference on small inputs. Rabin–Karp checks candidate matches against the original text rather than treating equal hashes as proof.

There are runnable examples and pytest tests. The repo leaves out assignment sheets, marking material and private course resources; it is meant to show the algorithms and my implementation work.

The source is advanced-string-algorithms, with additional notes in ALGORITHMS.md. Before using any of it for large-scale indexing I’d benchmark the real workload and replace the intentionally simple construction steps.

title: 字符串算法课结束后，我还留着哪些代码
description: 把以前写的字符串算法重新整理成独立仓库：Z匹配、BWT、后缀树、Rabin–Karp，还有那些不该被隐藏的实现限制。
content:
整理以前的算法课代码时，我不太想把每个作业文件原样扔上GitHub。课程已经结束了，有些代码能运行，但如果不把设计思路、复杂度和边界情况说明白，别人看不懂，我隔一段时间也未必记得为什么这么写。

后来我把几个字符串算法整理成了独立Python仓库。里面有四组东西：


  Z相关的精确匹配，包含从右向左匹配的跳跃预处理
  BWT和backward search，在索引上尝试一次编辑的近似匹配
  Ukkonen后缀树，以及从树里提取LCP数组
  Rabin–Karp滚动哈希，搭配Miller–Rabin素性测试


先讲清楚它不是什么

这是拿来展示算法实现和实验的仓库，不是生产级全文检索引擎。比如BWT部分为了让实现容易读，后缀数组构造仍然用比较直观的方法；Z匹配实现里的位移预处理有O(m²)的成本。如果只写“高效字符串匹配”，就把最重要的限制藏起来了。

后缀树也是一样。Ukkonen算法最容易讲得很玄，但写代码时真正会反复出错的是active point、suffix link和skip/count如何更新。比起只给一个理论上的时间复杂度，我更在意用小输入把这些状态跑对。

测试怎么安排

我给BWT近似匹配分别覆盖替换、插入、删除和交换四种单步编辑；后缀树的LCP结果拿一个朴素参考实现对照；滚动哈希不仅检查命中位置，也要处理哈希相同但原文不同的情况。

仓库里保留了运行例子和pytest测试。课程作业的说明、评分材料和其他不该公开的资源没有放进去。

代码在advanced-string-algorithms，实现笔记在ALGORITHMS.md。以后真要拿去处理大规模文本，我会先重做索引构建和性能评估，不会直接拿课程版的复杂度推断实际吞吐。

title: Two J1900 boxes and an N1: why I don't need more production servers
description: Two J1900 boxes, a Debian N1 and a VPS. Before finding more services to run, I need to decide what should stay online and what should remain disposable.
content:
I recently got two older J1900 machines working again. There’s also an N1 box running Debian, and the VPS that already hosts my public services. Having spare hardware brought back a familiar question: what else can I run on it?

This time I want to answer a different question first: which things need to survive when one of those machines stops working?

Not every box needs to run a website

My public sites already run on a VPS with HTTPS, automated deployment and monitoring. Replicating every production service at home isn’t automatically useful. A home connection has a changing public address, and power, disks and router restarts introduce failure modes I don’t control as easily.

For now I see the larger J1900 as a backup or standby box, the other J1900 as an isolated place to experiment, and the N1 as a small Debian/Linux test node. These are roles I’m working towards, not a claim that failover or a production backup is already implemented. Some machines can simply stay off.

The restore matters more than the backup

I want to write down exactly what would happen if the VPS or one of the disks failed:


  What data exists in only one place?
  Can I restore a database and the files that belong to it on a clean machine?
  How do I still get in over SSH when the home IP changes?
  Which jobs need a schedule and which should run only on demand?
  Will an alert describe a new failure, or repeat the same message all day?


A working Debian install doesn’t answer any of those questions.

Keeping the useful parts of older projects

My homelab network automation and edge fleet operations repositories are sanitized reconstructions of earlier tooling, not claims about the current machines.

The ideas that still seem worth carrying forward are stateful alerts, consecutive checks before acting, tight limits on automated operations, and dry-run by default. I’ll document an actual restore exercise when I’ve completed one. That’s a more useful result than a list of boxes I happen to own.

title: 有了两台J1900和一台N1，反而不能什么都往上放
description: 家里有两台J1900和一台N1，另外还有VPS。机器多了以后，我反而需要先想清楚哪些东西值得一直开着。
content:
最近整理家里的旧机器，两台J1900都能用了，N1盒子也刷好了Debian。手里还有一台VPS。以前机器不够，想的是“还能跑点什么”；现在几台设备空着，最先想到的反而是别把它们都变成需要照看的服务器。

我把它们分成三个角色：已经在提供服务的机器、可以接手服务的备份机器、拿来试错的机器。这个划分还在调整，并不是已经搭好了一套高可用集群。

不想让所有机器都承担生产任务

真正对外提供的网站在VPS上。域名、HTTPS、自动部署和监控已经有了，在家里复制一整套不一定有意义。家庭宽带的公网地址可能变化，断电、路由器重启、磁盘故障也更难控制。

J1900main目前更适合作为备份或备用环境。另一台J1900可以做独立的实验节点，N1暂时留作轻量Linux服务或网络实验。它们不必都24小时开机，也不需要为了“利用率”硬塞应用。

这也改变了我对Homelab的想法：重要的不是机器数量，而是坏掉一台时我知不知道会损失什么。

先把恢复流程写出来

备份不是多拷贝一份文件就算完成。我现在更想检查这几个问题：


  哪些数据只有一份？配置、数据库、上传文件分别放在哪里？
  备份能否在另一台机器上真正恢复？还是只能看到一个压缩包？
  SSH要通过哪个入口进入？主机公网地址变化时怎么办？
  哪些任务需要定时执行，哪些设备只在测试时开机？
  告警出问题时要告诉我什么，避免每隔几分钟重复发同一句话？


这些还是待完成的工作，不会因为机器已经装好Debian就自动解决。

旧项目还有用

我以前写过iKuai网络自动化和Linux节点巡检。公开仓库是脱敏后的重构版本，原来的部署已结束或变化，不代表现在家里这几台机器已经跑上了那些工具。

但里面有些思路仍然适用：连续多次检查后再告警、把状态存下来、限制每次自动处理的范围，危险动作先dry-run。接下来我会拿这些原则整理新设备，而不是把旧脚本原样搬过去。

等真正完成一次从备份到恢复的演练，再单独记录结果。相比展示一张摆满设备的图，我更想知道某一台突然开不了机时，自己能不能恢复。

title: Study Kit gets school mail and attendance, and asks before it changes anything
description: Study Kit 1.5.0 can optionally read your school mail and attendance. Anything that changes something shows you a full preview first and runs only after you confirm. Attendance reads two weeks in seconds without a browser, and students who never open a terminal can connect it by asking their AI app.
content:
Monash Study Kit used to read only Moodle and Ed. I had been using mail and attendance on my private deployment for a while, and 1.5.0, released on 31 October, brings them into the public version. Both are optional; nothing changes until you connect them.

The big difference from earlier releases is that it can now change things for the first time. Drafting mail, sending a draft, archiving and checking in to a class cannot be taken back if they go wrong. So this post is mostly about how those actions are kept in check, plus a few trade-offs I made so that students would actually use it.

Anything that changes something takes two steps

The AI cannot run a write in one step. It first calls a prepare tool and gets the full preview: recipients, Bcc, body and attachments, the label change, or the class and the code. The preview is stored as a ticket together with its SHA-256:

body = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
digest = hashlib.sha256(body.encode()).hexdigest()


To run it, the AI has to send the ticket ID, that hash and user_confirmed=true. The server’s instructions tell it to show the preview as it is and never confirm on the user’s behalf. A ticket expires after 10 minutes and works once. It is marked as executing before Gmail is contacted, so two clicks at the same time cannot send two emails. Before a draft is sent, its content is checked again, and a draft that changed after the preview is refused.

Failures come in two kinds. If a check fails before anything is sent, the ticket is marked rejected and you know nothing went out. If the request itself fails, it is marked unknown and is never retried by itself; you look at the mailbox first. Check-in is only prepared when you say you actually attended, and never for a class that has not started or is already done.

At first I left these writes off until the user turned them on in the settings. That felt broken in practice: a student logs in, asks the AI to archive a message, and the AI says it cannot. What actually protects the student is the two-step flow, not a switch. So in 1.5.0 they are on after login, and the switches stay for anyone who wants them off. The decision is written down in ADR 0004. Moodle and Ed are still read-only.

Each remote app picks what it gets

Remote mode in 1.4.0 had a single monash scope, so until now the remote server simply refused mail and attendance. Opening them up directly would have let a ChatGPT you paired last week read your whole mailbox without you knowing.

Now the pairing page shows a checkbox for each part the server owner has turned on: read-only ones start ticked, actions start unticked. The choice is stored with the authorization code and the tokens and survives refresh. Every call intersects it with the server’s current settings, so turning something off on the server takes it away from every app at once. Tokens from before 1.5.0 were set to monash when the database was upgraded, so old apps gain nothing. Tickets and background jobs belong to one client, so one app cannot run an action another app prepared.

Attendance without a browser

The attendance portal is an ASP.NET page where you switch days with a #daySel menu. My Chrome extension has always opened the page, switched to the day and run a JavaScript parser. Doing that in the background meant starting a headless browser and switching day by day, which is heavy for something that runs several times a day.

Switching days did not seem to load anything new; it only showed the matching dayPanel_<date> block. So every day was probably already in the HTML. I wrote a Python version of the parser that only looks inside that day’s block, and fetched the page once with the cookies saved at login.

A guess is not enough to ship, so there are two layers of comparison. In the tests, several differently structured pages go through the original JavaScript in a real browser and through the Python version, and the rows must match field by field, including the label text. There is also monash attendance probe, which reads the real portal both ways and prints only counts and whether they match, never course content. On the Malaysia campus portal, all 15 days it offers matched, and the page is 5 KB. So the fast read is on by default, and it falls back to the browser whenever the page looks different.

The first probe on my Mac failed with CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED. The portal most likely does not send its intermediate certificate; Chrome fetches it by itself, Python does not. The fix was truststore, which makes Python use the operating system’s verifier, and macOS fills in the missing certificate the same way Chrome does. Verification stays on the whole time.

When to read changed too. Instead of every hour, reads follow the timetable: weekday mornings at 8, and 15 minutes after each class you have not checked in to. Nothing runs at night, at weekends or for classes already done. I do not know yet how long the portal login lasts, so the program records each login, each successful read and the first expiry, and I will decide on a keepalive once there is data.

No terminal for students

Once it worked, there was another problem. Connecting Gmail meant creating a Google Cloud project, enabling the API, downloading a JSON file and typing a command. For most students that is so much work that Claude’s built-in Gmail connector is simply easier.

I did two things. First, the package now includes a desktop app client made just for the public version. Google designs these files to ship with the program; it only tells Google which app is asking and cannot read anyone’s mail. GitHub’s push protection still flagged it and I had to allow it by hand. The cost is the “this app isn’t verified” warning, and a limit of 100 users for an app Google has not reviewed, which is fine for a group of friends.

Second, a new tool, start_school_service_setup. A student says “connect my school email” in their AI app, and it installs the missing packages into the running install, opens the sign-in window and leaves only the sign-in to them. When it is done it tells the AI app to refresh its tool list. The tool costs about 145 tokens per conversation, so it hides itself once both parts are connected. The parameters of the original 17 tools are pinned by a hash in the tests, and none of them changed.

Takeaways


  Writes are kept safe by the flow, not by a switch: a full preview, a single-use ticket bound to that content, the user’s confirmation, and no automatic retries.
  When an existing remote grant could gain a new ability, do not let it grow on its own. Ask the user to choose again.
  Before replacing a parser that already works, run old and new side by side on real data, then make the new one the default.
  When certificate verification fails, find out why. Do not turn verification off.
  A feature is not done until an ordinary student can get through the steps to connect it.

title: Study Kit 接上学校邮箱和考勤：会改东西的都先给你看
description: Study Kit 1.5.0 可以选择接上学校邮箱和考勤。会改东西的操作都先给你看完整预览，你确认了才执行；考勤不开浏览器，几秒读完两周；不会用命令行的同学在 AI 里说一声就能接上。
content:
Monash Study Kit 原来只读 Moodle 和 Ed。邮箱和考勤我一直在自己的私人部署上用，10 月 31 日发布的 1.5.0 把它们搬进了公开版。两部分都是可选的，接上之前什么都不会多。

这次和以前最大的不同是：它第一次能改东西了。起草邮件、发草稿、归档、签到，做错了都收不回来。所以这篇主要讲这些操作是怎么管住的，还有几处为了让同学用得下去做的取舍。

会改东西的，都分两步

AI 不能一步就执行写操作。它先调用 prepare，拿到一份完整预览：收件人、密送、正文、附件，或者要改的标签，或者是哪节课、哪个签到码。这份预览连同它的 SHA-256 存成一张凭据：

body = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
digest = hashlib.sha256(body.encode()).hexdigest()


执行时要带上凭据编号、这个哈希，还要 user_confirmed=true。服务器给 AI 的说明里写着：预览要原样给用户看，不能替用户确认。凭据 10 分钟过期，只能用一次。执行前先把它标成“正在执行”再去联系 Gmail，所以同时点两次也不会发出两封。发送草稿前还会再核对一次草稿内容，预览之后被改过就拒绝。

出错也分两种。执行前的检查没过，记成“已拒绝”，可以确定什么都没发出去；真正发请求时出错，记成“结果未知”，不会自动重试，要先去邮箱里看看到底发没发。签到只有你说自己实际到课了才会准备，而且不能给还没开始或已经签过的课提交。

一开始我让这些写操作默认关着，要用户自己去设置里打开。后来发现这样很别扭：同学登录完问 AI“帮我把这封归档”，AI 说做不到，看起来像坏了。真正起保护作用的是上面那个两步流程，不是开关。所以 1.5.0 改成登录以后就打开，开关留着给不想要的人关。这个决定写进了 ADR 0004。Moodle 和 Ed 还是只读，没有变。

远程的每个软件自己选

1.4.0 的远程模式只有一个 monash 权限，所以之前的版本干脆整组拒绝邮箱和考勤。直接放开的话，已经配对过的 ChatGPT 会在你不知道的情况下突然能读整个邮箱。

现在配对页上，服务器开了的功能各有一个勾选框：只读的默认勾上，写操作默认不勾。勾了什么就存进授权码和令牌，刷新令牌时一起带过去。每次调用时，再和服务器当前的设置取一次交集，服务器上关掉某项，所有软件马上就用不了。1.5.0 之前配对的令牌在数据库升级时补的是 monash，所以旧软件不会多出任何权限。凭据和后台任务也按客户端分开，一个软件准备的操作，另一个软件执行不了。

考勤不开浏览器

考勤门户是一个 ASP.NET 页面，日期用 #daySel 下拉框切换。我的 Chrome 插件一直是让浏览器打开页面、切到那天、再跑一段 JavaScript 解析。放到后台定时跑，每次都要起一个无头浏览器，一天一天地切，很重。

我注意到切日期时页面并不会重新请求，只是把对应的 dayPanel_<日期> 显示出来。那么所有日期很可能本来就在 HTML 里。于是写了一个 Python 版的解析器，只在当天那个区块里找，用登录时保存的 cookie 直接请求一次页面。

光凭猜不能就这么上线，所以做了两层对照。测试里用几种不同结构的页面，让浏览器跑原来的 JS、Python 跑新的解析，逐条比较，连显示文字都要一样。另外加了一个 monash attendance probe，在真实门户上把两种读法各跑一遍，只输出数量和对不对得上，不输出课程内容。在马来西亚校区的门户上，门户提供的 15 天全部一致，页面只有 5 KB。所以快速读取默认打开了，页面结构对不上时会自动退回浏览器。

第一次在 Mac 上跑 probe 时报了 CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED。门户服务器大概没把中间证书发全，Chrome 会自己去补，Python 自带的校验不会。最后用 truststore 让 Python 走系统的证书校验，macOS 会像 Chrome 一样补上。校验一直是开着的，没有为了能跑通去关掉它。

读的时间也换了思路。不按钟点每小时跑，而是按课表：工作日早上 8 点读一次，每节还没签到的课开始 15 分钟后再读一次。晚上、周末和已经签过的课都不跑。登录能维持多久还不知道，所以程序会记下每次登录、每次成功和第一次过期的时间，等有了数据再决定要不要续期。

不让同学开终端

功能做完后有一个问题：接 Gmail 要自己去 Google Cloud 建项目、开 API、下载一个 JSON，再在终端里输命令。这对大多数同学来说太难了，难到不如直接用 Claude 自带的 Gmail 连接器。

我做了两件事。第一，安装包里带了一个公开版专用的桌面应用客户端。按 Google 的设计，桌面应用的这个文件本来就随程序公开，它只告诉 Google 是哪个应用在请求授权，拿不到任何人的邮件；GitHub 的推送保护还是会拦一下，要手动放行。代价是授权页会显示“尚未验证此应用”，而且没审核的应用最多 100 个用户，对朋友圈子够用。

第二，加了一个工具 start_school_service_setup。同学在 AI 里说“帮我接上学校邮箱”，它在后台把缺的组件装进现在的环境，然后在电脑上打开登录窗口，同学只要登录。接好以后通知 AI 软件刷新工具列表。这个工具每次对话多占约 145 个 token，所以两样都接好以后它会自己隐藏。原来 17 个工具的参数在测试里是用哈希锁住的，这次一个都没改。

小结


  写操作的安全靠流程，不靠开关：完整预览、绑定内容的一次性凭据、用户确认、出错不重试。
  给已有的远程授权加新能力时，旧的授权不能跟着变大，要让用户重新选。
  想换掉一个验证过的解析器，先在真实数据上把新旧两个对照一遍，再默认打开。
  证书校验不过时，去找为什么不过，不要关掉校验。
  功能做好了还不够，接上它的步骤也要是普通同学能走完的。

title: Letting ChatGPT reach Study Kit, for one person only
description: Study Kit 1.4.0 can now be reached from ChatGPT and Claude on the web. It stays a server for one person: a pairing code from your own terminal, a short list of callback addresses, rotating tokens, and only the tools that read.
content:
Monash Study Kit syncs your own Moodle and Ed to your computer and lets an AI app search them over MCP. Claude Desktop and Claude Code start it as a local program and talk to it over stdio. ChatGPT and Claude on the web or phone cannot do that. They live on someone else’s server, so they need an HTTPS address to call.

Version 1.4.0 came out on 30 October with an optional monash remote mode for this. This post is about how it is locked down, because a URL on the internet that can read your Moodle is not something to get wrong.

One person, their own data

I already decided not to host Study Kit for everyone. That would mean keeping every student’s Moodle login and Ed token on my server, and one break in would expose all of them. The docs explain the same reason.

So remote mode is for the owner of the data only. You run it on your own server, or on your own laptop behind a free Cloudflare quick tunnel, and it serves your synced files to your own AI apps. Setup never starts it, and installing or updating the package does not open any port. Nothing listens until you run monash remote serve yourself.

The server also refuses to bind anywhere except loopback:

def make_server(addr, con):
    if addr[0] not in {"127.0.0.1", "localhost"}:
        raise ValueError("Bind remote MCP on loopback behind an HTTPS reverse proxy")


HTTPS comes from nginx or the tunnel in front of it. Every request is checked for a Host and Origin that match the public address you gave, so a web page that points its own domain at your machine (DNS rebinding) gets a 403.

A pairing code instead of a password

ChatGPT and Claude connect with OAuth, which normally means a sign in page with a password. I did not want to add accounts to a tool for one person. Instead the sign in page asks for a code you get from your own terminal:

$ monash remote pair
Pairing code: 3F9A-0C21-B7E4
Valid for 10 minutes, single use.


The database keeps only its SHA-256 hash. A right code is used up at once. Five wrong codes close the window, and you run pair again. If nobody has opened a window, the page says so and does not accept anything. Someone who finds your URL cannot get in without also being at your keyboard in the last ten minutes.

Who is allowed to connect

MCP apps register themselves before signing in, and the protocol says registration needs no login. That means anyone can register. Two things keep that from mattering.

First, a registration is only accepted when every callback address is on a short list: the exact OAuth callback paths on claude.ai, claude.com and chatgpt.com, matched on the whole host with no port, query or fragment. A client that wants its code sent anywhere else is turned away at the door, so a stolen code can only travel back to Claude or ChatGPT. You can add one exact extra address with a flag, never a pattern.

Second, registrations are capped at 50. When it is full, clients that registered more than an hour ago and never got a token are cleared out. A client that is really in use always has a refresh token, so it stays.

The rest is standard OAuth for public clients:


  PKCE with S256 is required. The code is only exchanged when the verifier hashes to the challenge from the sign in.
  The access token lasts one hour. The refresh token lasts 30 days and is replaced every time it is used, so an old one stops working.
  Tokens are stored as hashes in secrets/remote-mcp.db, which is created with mode 0600.
  monash remote revoke --all deletes every client, code and token and closes any open pairing window.


Only the tools that read

Locally Study Kit has 18 tools. Two of them start a Moodle login or a sync, and those need a browser and your password on the machine itself. Remote mode drops them from the tool list and refuses them by name if an app calls them anyway:

if spec and len(spec) > 3 and not spec[3]:
    return {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": msg.get("id"), "error": {
        "code": -32602, "message": "Run login or sync on the server's own terminal"}}


So the 16 query tools are all a token can reach. With a stolen token someone could read your course files until it expires or you revoke it, which is bad, but they could not log in as you or change anything on Moodle or Ed. Study Kit has no tool that submits, posts or attempts a quiz, locally or remotely.

How I checked it

tests/test_remote.py has 22 tests that run the whole flow on one machine with made up data: discovery from a 401, registration, pairing, PKCE, token expiry and rotation, revoke, the callback list, bad hosts and origins, and refusing login and sync. One test opens a database in the older layout, before tokens were tied to the server address, to make sure tokens saved there still work after the upgrade.

On 30 October the 1.4.0 package from PyPI also went through the same sign in and query flow in a clean environment, using the real Claude and ChatGPT callback addresses. That check had no public domain. With my own domain and server, ChatGPT Plus can query my Moodle and Ed. The steps are on Host it yourself.

Takeaways


  A remote mode for a personal tool should stay personal. One owner, their own data, nothing started for them.
  A code from your own terminal replaces a whole account system when there is only one user.
  Check callback addresses when a client registers. After that, every later step can trust them.
  Decide which tools leave the machine. Anything that logs in or writes stays local.

title: 让 ChatGPT 也能用 Study Kit，但只给自己用
description: Study Kit 1.4.0 起，ChatGPT 和网页版 Claude 也能连上。它仍然只给一个人用：配对码从你自己的终端拿，回调地址只认几个，令牌会轮换，远程只开放只读的工具。
content:
Monash Study Kit 把你自己的 Moodle 和 Ed 同步到电脑上，让 AI 软件通过 MCP 去搜。Claude Desktop 和 Claude Code 是在本机把它当程序启动，用 stdio 通信。ChatGPT 和网页版、手机上的 Claude 做不到这一点，它们跑在别人的服务器上，只能去调一个 HTTPS 地址。

10 月 30 日发布的 1.4.0 加了一个可选的 monash remote 模式来解决这个问题。这篇讲它是怎么锁住的，因为一个能读你 Moodle 的公网地址，出错的代价很大。

只给一个人，只读自己的数据

我之前就决定不替所有人托管 Study Kit。那样我的服务器上会存着每个同学的 Moodle 登录和 Ed 令牌，被攻破一次就全部泄露。文档里也是这么解释的。

所以远程模式只给数据的主人自己用。你在自己的服务器上跑，或者在自己电脑上开一个 Cloudflare 免费的临时隧道，它把你同步好的资料提供给你自己的 AI 软件。setup 不会启动它，安装和更新也不会开任何端口。只有你自己运行 monash remote serve，它才开始监听。

服务器还拒绝绑定在本机回环以外的地址：

def make_server(addr, con):
    if addr[0] not in {"127.0.0.1", "localhost"}:
        raise ValueError("Bind remote MCP on loopback behind an HTTPS reverse proxy")


HTTPS 由前面的 nginx 或隧道负责。每个请求都会检查 Host 和 Origin 是否和你给的公网地址一致，所以别的网页把自己的域名指到你机器上（DNS rebinding）会直接拿到 403。

用配对码代替密码

ChatGPT 和 Claude 用 OAuth 连接，通常意味着要有一个输密码的登录页。一个只有一个人用的工具，我不想为它做账号系统。所以登录页要的是你在自己终端里拿到的码：

$ monash remote pair
Pairing code: 3F9A-0C21-B7E4
Valid for 10 minutes, single use.


数据库里只存它的 SHA-256 哈希。输对一次就作废。输错五次窗口就关掉，要重新运行 pair。没有打开的窗口时，页面会直接提示，什么都不接受。别人就算知道了你的地址，不在十分钟内坐在你的电脑前也进不来。

谁可以连进来

MCP 软件在登录之前会先自己注册，协议规定注册不需要登录。也就是说谁都能注册。有两点让这件事不要紧。

第一，只有回调地址全部在白名单上，注册才会被接受：claude.ai、claude.com 和 chatgpt.com 上那几条固定的 OAuth 回调路径，整个主机名完全匹配，不能带端口、查询串或片段。想把授权码发到别处的客户端在注册时就被拒了，所以就算授权码被截到，也只能回到 Claude 或 ChatGPT。可以用参数额外加一个精确的地址，但不能写通配。

第二，注册的客户端最多 50 个。满了以后，会清掉注册超过一小时、从来没换到过令牌的客户端。真正在用的客户端一定有刷新令牌，所以不会被清掉。

剩下的是公开客户端的标准 OAuth：


  必须用 PKCE（S256）。只有 verifier 算出来的哈希和登录时的 challenge 一致，授权码才能换令牌。
  访问令牌一小时过期。刷新令牌 30 天过期，每用一次就换新的，旧的立刻失效。
  令牌以哈希形式存在 secrets/remote-mcp.db，文件创建时权限就是 0600。
  monash remote revoke --all 删掉所有客户端、授权码和令牌，并关掉还开着的配对窗口。


远程只开放读的工具

本地的 Study Kit 有 18 个工具。其中两个会启动 Moodle 登录或同步，这需要在那台机器上开浏览器、输密码。远程模式把它们从工具列表里去掉，就算软件硬要按名字调用，也会被拒绝：

if spec and len(spec) > 3 and not spec[3]:
    return {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": msg.get("id"), "error": {
        "code": -32602, "message": "Run login or sync on the server's own terminal"}}


所以令牌能碰到的只有 16 个查询工具。令牌被偷的话，在它过期或被你撤销之前，对方能读你的课件，这当然不好，但他没法用你的身份登录，也改不了 Moodle 或 Ed 上的任何东西。不管本地还是远程，Study Kit 都没有提交作业、发帖或做测验的工具。

怎么验证的

tests/test_remote.py 里有 22 个测试，用编造的数据在一台机器上走完整个流程：从 401 开始的服务发现、注册、配对、PKCE、令牌过期和轮换、撤销、回调白名单、错误的 Host 和 Origin，以及拒绝登录和同步。有一个测试专门打开旧格式的数据库（令牌还没和服务器地址绑定的时候），确认升级以后之前存的令牌还能用。

10 月 30 日，PyPI 上的 1.4.0 包也在干净环境里用 Claude 和 ChatGPT 真实的回调地址走了一遍同样的登录和查询流程。那次测试没有公网域名。用我自己的域名和服务器，ChatGPT Plus 可以查我的 Moodle 和 Ed。具体步骤在自己托管。

小结


  个人工具的远程模式就应该一直是个人的。一个主人，只有他自己的数据，不替别人启动任何东西。
  只有一个用户的时候，一个从自己终端拿的码就能代替整套账号系统。
  回调地址在客户端注册时就查清楚，后面每一步都能放心用。
  想清楚哪些工具可以离开这台机器。会登录或会写东西的，都留在本地。

title: From 662 official pages to 3,100, without losing any when a crawl fails
description: Monash Hub's guides went from 662 official pages to about 3,100 in one weekend. How the list is built from two sitemaps, what gets left out, and why a failed fetch no longer takes a page down.
content:
Besides the Handbook, Monash Hub keeps a copy of Monash’s official student pages: enrolment, exams, visas, fees, graduation. It translates them into Chinese, searches them and answers questions from them. Until 25 October that copy had 662 pages, found by walking links out from a few hub pages.

This post covers the weekend I widened it to both Monash sites, and the failures that came with it.

Read the sitemap instead of walking links

Walking from hubs only finds what menus link to. Both Monash sites publish sitemaps, and a sitemap lists every page, including ones no menu points at. So the crawler now reads them (#215):


  monash.edu.my: the whole site.
  monash.edu: the sitemaps of students, admissions and the IT, Business, Engineering and Science faculties, keeping only /students, /admissions and each faculty’s current-students section.


A whole-site sitemap is mostly not for students. One regex drops news, events, alumni, staff profiles, open day pages, sign-in and feedback forms, verification files and attached PDFs and images. What was left was about 3,100 pages.

A page that was already listed stays even when no sitemap has it, as long as it still has text. A page Monash moved keeps its slug and its translations at the new address.

Then take out what is not guidance

The first full list was too wide. The 选课与课程规划 category held 1,331 pages, because every faculty page defaulted to enrolment. Three passes cleaned it up:


  School pages that are not guidance (#221): 174 pages of leadership lists, rankings, competitions and their galleries, study-trip posts from 2005 to 2017, lab pages and test copies. A school page now counts as enrolment only when its address is about courses.
  Pages students cannot open (#222): five eExam pages answer “Access Denied” even to a signed-in student, so they leave instead of keeping old text. The fee calculator is listed as a link, because the page only forwards to an app.
  Pages about years that are over (#223): 152 pages, such as OSHC price lists from 2016 to 2025 and past principal dates.


The third one is a rule, so it keeps working next January:

COMMENCEMENT_YEARS = 6  # five years for the longest double degree, one more for a semester off

def outdated(url, title, year=None):
    year = year or date.today().year
    years = [int(y) for y in YEAR.findall(f"{urlparse(url).path} {title}")]
    if not years:
        return False
    if BY_COMMENCEMENT.search(f"{url} {title}"):   # course maps, "commenced"
        return max(years) <= year - COMMENCEMENT_YEARS
    return max(years) < year


Course maps are the exception. A student follows the map of the year they started, so in 2026 the maps from 2021 on stay. The YEAR pattern skips course codes like C2001 and “students who commenced from 2014”, which are not about a past year.

Later a staff tool turned up too: “Welcome to the Connect Tutor” is Monash Connect’s tool for checking an email reply before sending it (#230). It was in the support guides because it is in the sitemap.

A failed fetch used to hide a page

Before this change, any failed fetch set the page’s status to error. That took it off the guides, search, key dates and the assistant until a later fetch worked. One timeout or one bot challenge hid a page whose text was still right.

That stopped being rare. On 25 October, Monash Malaysia’s site started refusing the server’s address. A full re-crawl that night was refused on 359 pages. Under the old rule all of them would have gone dark.

Now only an answer about the page itself takes it down (#211):

def record_failure(db, page, message, *, gone=False):
    page.fetch_error = message[:2000]
    if gone or not page.content_hash:      # 404 or 410, or nothing stored yet
        page.status = "error"
        page.last_checked = datetime.now(UTC)
    elif page.status == "error":           # hidden by the old rule; bring it back
        page.status = "ok"


A 403 or a timeout keeps the last good copy, and last_checked keeps the date it was last read, because that is the date readers see. fetch_error makes the page due on the next run.

Two more cases looked like success but were not:


  A removed page often redirects to the section above it or to the home page. That landing page reads fine, so it would have replaced the real text quietly. A redirect to a parent is now recorded as a failure.
  A long page that suddenly reads short keeps its last good copy. A page that is short on Monash’s site too, like a hub of links, is stored, as long as there is no longer copy to keep (#217).


When the site refuses the server

While monash.edu.my refuses the VPS, its pages can be read on another computer and handed to the server as a harvest file. The server stores them with the same code it uses for its own fetches (deployment/crawl.sh official-harvest FILE).

The first harvest broke in a new way. A run stopped mid-write tore the file, and reading stopped at the tear, so the server loaded none of 680 pages. Each page is now its own gzip member, and the reader skips a torn member and goes on from the next one (#216). It also reads one page at a time, since 723 pages held in memory went past the crawler container’s 2 GB.

Limits on the Handbook side too

The same weekend added limits to the weekly Handbook crawl (#212):


  One run marks at most 25 units inactive, or 2% of its targets if that is more. A Handbook answering 404 for everything would otherwise take every unit off the site for a week.
  A run stops after 30 failures in a row and records why. Before, a Handbook that was down cost three attempts for each of 5,000 units.
  A failed run, or one where more than 5% of targets failed, sends one email a day. /api/health shows the last run of each kind.


Takeaways


  A sitemap is a better list than a crawl from the menu, but it lists everything, so the filter matters more than the fetcher.
  Write “out of date” as a rule with today’s year in it, not as a list of pages.
  Only take content down when the source says it is gone. A refusal or a timeout says nothing about the page.

title: 官方页面从 662 页到 3100 页，抓取失败也不丢
description: 一个周末，Monash Hub 收录的官方页面从 662 页变成 3100 页左右。页面列表怎么从两个网站的 sitemap 来，哪些页要剔掉，以及抓取失败为什么不再让页面下线。
content:
除了 Handbook，Monash Hub 还存了一份 Monash 官方的学生页面：选课、考试、签证、学费、毕业。网站会把它们翻成中文、能搜索，站内助手也从这里找答案。到 10 月 25 日之前，这份副本只有 662 页，是从几个入口页顺着链接走出来的。

这篇讲那个周末我把范围扩到 Monash 两个网站的全部学生页面，以及跟着出现的问题。

读 sitemap，不再顺着链接走

从入口页顺着链接走，只能找到菜单里链到的页面。Monash 两个网站都有 sitemap，里面列了每一页，包括没有任何菜单指向的页。所以爬虫现在直接读 sitemap（#215）：


  monash.edu.my：整个网站。
  monash.edu：students、admissions，以及 IT、商科、工程、理科几个学院的 sitemap，只留 /students、/admissions 和各学院的 current-students 部分。


整站的 sitemap 大部分不是给学生看的。一个正则把新闻、活动、校友、教职工主页、开放日、登录和反馈表单、验证文件，以及附件里的 PDF 和图片都去掉。剩下大约 3100 页。

已经收录的页面，就算不在 sitemap 里，只要还有正文就保留。Monash 换了地址的页面，保留原来的 slug 和翻译，挪到新地址。

再把不是指南的页面去掉

第一版列表太宽了。“选课与课程规划”这一类有 1331 页，因为学院的页面默认都归到选课。后面分三次清理：


  学院里不是指南的页面（#221）：174 页，包括领导名单、排名、竞赛和相册、2005 到 2017 年的游学帖子、实验室页面和测试副本。学院页面现在只有地址和课程有关时才算选课。
  学生打不开的页面（#222）：5 个 eExam 页面就算登录了也返回 “Access Denied”，所以直接去掉，不再留旧内容。学费计算器只是跳转到一个应用，改成一个链接。
  讲已经过去的年份的页面（#223）：152 页，比如 2016 到 2025 年的 OSHC 价目表、往年的校历。


第三条写成了规则，明年一月照样生效：

COMMENCEMENT_YEARS = 6  # 最长的双学位五年，再加一个学期休学

def outdated(url, title, year=None):
    year = year or date.today().year
    years = [int(y) for y in YEAR.findall(f"{urlparse(url).path} {title}")]
    if not years:
        return False
    if BY_COMMENCEMENT.search(f"{url} {title}"):   # 课程地图、“commenced”
        return max(years) <= year - COMMENCEMENT_YEARS
    return max(years) < year


课程地图是例外。学生一直按入学那年的课程地图走，所以 2026 年保留 2021 年以后的。YEAR 这个正则会跳过 C2001 这种课程代码，还有 “students who commenced from 2014” 这种写法，它们说的不是过去的某一年。

后来又发现一个员工工具：“Welcome to the Connect Tutor” 是 Monash Connect 给工作人员检查邮件回复用的（#230）。它在 sitemap 里，所以被放进了支持类指南。

以前一次抓取失败就会让页面下线

以前只要抓取失败，页面状态就变成 error，指南、搜索、重要日期和站内助手里都看不到它，直到下次抓成功。一次超时或者一次机器人验证，就能把内容还是对的页面藏起来。

这种情况后来不少见了。10 月 25 日起，Monash 马来西亚校区的网站开始拒绝服务器的 IP。当晚一次全量重抓，有 359 页被拒。按旧规则，这些页面会全部下线。

现在只有说明页面本身没了的回应才会让它下线（#211）：

def record_failure(db, page, message, *, gone=False):
    page.fetch_error = message[:2000]
    if gone or not page.content_hash:      # 404 或 410，或者还没存过内容
        page.status = "error"
        page.last_checked = datetime.now(UTC)
    elif page.status == "error":           # 被旧规则藏起来的，恢复
        page.status = "ok"


403 或者超时，保留上一份好的内容，last_checked 也不动，因为读者看到的“最后检查日期”应该是最后一次真正读到的时间。fetch_error 会让这一页在下次运行时优先重抓。

还有两种情况看起来成功了，其实没有：


  被删掉的页面常常跳转到上一级栏目或者首页。跳过去的页面看起来很正常，会悄悄替换掉原来的内容。现在跳到上级页面算失败。
  很长的页面突然只读到很短的内容，保留上一份好的。官网上本来就短的页面，比如一个只有链接的入口页，在没有更长的旧内容可留时照常存（#217）。


网站拒绝服务器的时候

monash.edu.my 拒绝 VPS 的这段时间，它的页面可以在另一台电脑上读，打包成一个 harvest 文件交给服务器。服务器用和自己抓取同一套代码存进去（deployment/crawl.sh official-harvest FILE）。

第一次 harvest 就出了新问题。一次运行在写文件中途被停掉，文件损坏了，读取到损坏的地方就停，结果服务器 680 页一页都没导入。现在每一页是一个独立的 gzip 成员，读的时候跳过损坏的那个，从下一个接着读（#216）。服务器也改成一页一页地读，因为 723 页一起放进内存，超过了爬虫容器的 2 GB。

Handbook 这边也加了上限

同一个周末，每周的 Handbook 抓取也加了几个上限（#212）：


  一次运行最多把 25 门课标成停开，目标多的时候按 2% 算。不然 Handbook 哪天对所有请求都返回 404，所有课程都会下线一周。
  连续失败 30 个就停下，并记下原因。以前 Handbook 挂了，5000 门课每门要试三次。
  运行失败，或者超过 5% 的目标失败，每天最多发一封邮件。/api/health 能看到每类抓取最近一次的结果。


小结


  sitemap 比顺着菜单爬全，但它什么都列，所以过滤规则比抓取本身更重要。
  “过时”要写成带当前年份的规则，不要写成一张页面清单。
  只有来源说页面没了，才把内容撤下。被拒绝或者超时，说明不了页面本身。


代码：coverage.py、discover.py、repository.py。更新日志：CHANGELOG.md。

title: Turning a bot's quote check into a package
description: The word-for-word check in my WeChat bot is now its own Python package with no dependencies. What it keeps and drops, why it does not use a second model as a judge, and how a release gets from a tag to PyPI.
content:
My WeChat Q&A bot lets a language model answer only with sentences copied from the passages it was given. Code checks each one before anything is sent. I wrote about why in A Q&A bot where the model is only allowed to quote.

That check lived inside the bot’s wxbot/rag.py, mixed up with retrieval, campus labels and WeChat formatting. This weekend I pulled it out into quotegate, a Python package on PyPI under MIT. This post is about what went into the package and what stayed out.

What it does

The model is told to reply with lines like [2] a sentence, copied. check() reads those lines and keeps a quote only when it really is in passage 2 and still reads right on its own:

from quotegate import Passage, check

passages = [
    Passage("Special consideration\nApply online within two working days of the due date. "
            "This must include supporting documents.", title="Special consideration"),
]
reply = "[1] Apply online within two working days\n[1] This must include supporting documents"

result = check(reply, passages)
result.status    # "ok"
result.kept      # [Quote(passage=1, text="Apply online within two working days of the due date.", start=22, end=75)]
result.dropped   # [Dropped(passage=1, quote="This must include supporting documents.", reason="needs context")]


The first quote is widened to the whole sentence it sits in. The second is in the passage, but it starts with “This”, which leans on a sentence the reader will not see, so it is dropped with a reason.

When status is not "ok", nothing from the model should be sent. The four other statuses say why: the model said it does not know, it quoted nothing, none of its quotes are in the passages, or the ones that are cannot be read alone. The bot forwards those questions to me.

What gets dropped

Most of the rules came from real replies the bot almost sent:


  
    
      Reason
      Example
    
  
  
    
      not found
      A paraphrase, or a quote credited to the wrong passage
    
    
      needs context
      Starts with “This must…”, “However”, “不，”; ends with “:” or “；并且”
    
    
      list item
      ”- you must contact ISP” under “If you don’t meet any of the requirements above:”
    
    
      table row
      “Oct intake | OCT-MY-01 | 6 Jan”, without the header row
    
    
      past year
      “From 2022 exams are online”, read in 2026
    
    
      a question
      The passage’s own FAQ question
    
  


Models do not always follow the format either. The line parser accepts 【2†L9-L12】, full-width brackets, a bullet in front and a colon after the number, because I saw all of them from free models.

Sentence splitting needed two switches. A line break ends a sentence by default, since in web pages it is usually a heading or a list item. WeChat articles and PDF text break lines mid-sentence, so those passages are marked soft_breaks=True. A latin full stop only ends a sentence before whitespace, so “50.0” and “monash.edu” stay whole.

What stayed out

No model. A popular way to check a RAG answer is to ask a second model whether each claim is supported, like Ragas faithfulness. That gives a score after the fact, and the judge can be wrong both ways. In the bot, a second model checking sentences missed some added steps and cut correct ones. A string check gives the same answer every time and cannot be talked round.

No network and no dependencies. The whole package is about 290 lines of standard library Python. It takes about 0.3 ms to check four quotes against five 500-character passages.

No retrieval, no prompts beyond a starting point. quotegate.prompts has an English and a Chinese system prompt that ask for the format, but finding the right passages is the caller’s job. The README says plainly what the package cannot do: a true sentence that answers a different question still passes.

Everything that was specific to the bot became a setting in Rules: lengths, the connective patterns, the current year for the past-year check, and a checks list for your own rules. The bot’s campus sorting is not in the package at all.

From a tag to PyPI

I wanted releases to be boring:


  Every push runs the tests on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows with Python 3.10 and 3.13, and runs ruff.
  A separate job builds the wheel, installs it into a clean virtual environment and runs the README example. That catches a package that passes its tests but ships without a file.
  Pushing a v0.1.0 tag runs release.yml. It checks that the tag matches __version__, that CHANGELOG.md has that section, and that the tagged commit is on main. Then it runs the tests again and uploads with PyPI Trusted Publishing, so no token is stored anywhere. The GitHub Release is made from the changelog section.


0.1.0 went out this way on 26 October.

What is next

The bot still has its own copy of the check in wxbot/rag.py. Moving it onto the package is the next step, so the two cannot drift apart.

Takeaways


  Pull code out when it has a clear input and output, and leave the parts that know about your product behind.
  Write down what the package does not stop. For a safety check that matters more than the feature list.
  Check the release in the release workflow: version, changelog and branch, then a clean install.
